slides: Equal ratios. A short lesson, but one of the most important in the whole course.

slides.say: We're going to learn a technique that follows us through the whole quantitative section. In word problems, in geometry, and in algebra too. Many questions rest on one idea, the same rate in two different cases.
at: the same rate in two different cases

slides.say: For example, every box holds the same number of pens. Or a machine works at a steady pace. When the rate stays the same, the two cases have equal ratios. The easiest way to learn it is on an example, so let's go straight to the questions. I'll see you in the next video.
at: the two cases have equal ratios
